newsitem.title: USA: MK Rail pays off note at a discount.
newsitem.headline: MK Rail pays off note at a discount.

text.p: MK Rail Corp said Tuesday it completed a debt-reduction transaction by repaying a note owed to Morrison Knudsen Corp at a discount to face value.
In the transaction, MK Rail said, it repaid $57.3 million of debt, including accrued interest, for $34.6 million.
In conjunction with the note repayment, Morrison Knudsen Corp expects to emerge from bankruptcy and merge with Washington Construction Inc.
As part of its bankruptcy plan, Morrison Knudsen plans to distribute its 63 percent ownership of MK Rail stock, about 11.1 million shares, to its creditors and shareholders.
The stock distribution is expected to occur during the first week of October, at which time Morrison Knudsen would no longer be an MK Rail stockholder, the company added.

MK Rail said its debt will total about $65 million at the end of the third quarter, down from $120 million at the beginning of the year. During the same period, stockholders' equity will have increased to about $115 million from $94.5 million and book value per share of common stock to about $6.55 from $5.38.
In addition, the company said, it expects the note payment to reduce annual interest expense by about $1 million.

"This debt-reduction transaction represents the final step in the turnaround plan that we articulated at the beginning of this year," said John C. (Jack) Pope, the company's chairman. MK Rail is now profitable and has a strong balance sheet.

Also, Robert S. Miller Jr. will resign from the MK Rail board, effective September 11, the company said. Miller had been the chairman of Morrison Knudsen and would be the vice chairman of Morrison Knudsen following its merger with Washington Construction. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
